subject: Mosaic Health — SLO / topology deck and next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@mosaichealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Mosaic Health — SLO / topology deck and next steps

Hi Julia / Mosaic Platform Team,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — really appreciated the candid discussion about where you are seeing inference-related cost spikes and the operational fragility when traffic bursts. Quick recap of what we heard, and a proposed set of next steps so we can get you a POC cluster that matches the production workload: 

Pain points we captured
- 95th/99th latency spikes at peak times (~200–350 ms currently for short text classification flows) causing downstream timeouts
- High per-token cost on large models when traffic bursts (billing unpredictability)
- Lack of predictable autoscaling for KV-cache-heavy prompts; cold-starts create latency outliers

Goals you stated
- P95 inference latency target: <= 120ms for 2–4 token outputs, P99 <= 200ms (for decisioning endpoints)
- Baseline throughput target: sustained 60 qps with capacity to burst to 200 qps for 2–3 minutes
- Evaluate both hosted and private VPC deployment options for HIPAA-adjacent traffic; SOC2 evidence required before pilot

Technical notes from call
- Primary model family: fine-tuned LlamaX-13B variant (quantized to 4-bit for cost) with typical prompt length of 128 tokens and average response length ~32 tokens
- Typical request distribution: 60% short-context (<256 tokens), 30% medium (256–1024), 10% long (>1024) — KV cache hit patterns are important
- Preferred topology: private VPC for PHI-adjacent endpoints + hosted fallbacks for overflow; we discussed dedicated GPU pools vs shared hosted with routing rules

Attachments included in this message
- mosaic_slo_topology_deck_v1.pdf — slides with topology sketches and baseline perf targets
- mosaic_slo_matrix.csv — a simple SLO/traffic matrix and test plan
- call_recording_20290411.mp3 — recording of today’s call

Proposed next steps (timeline + owners)
1) Security checklist & SOC2 evidence request (you) — Julia: please confirm the most recent point-of-contact for security artifacts by EOD Friday
2) POC cluster spec & quote (Redwood) — Priya / Sean: we’ll produce a POC spec that matches the burst profile above by Tuesday 4/16
3) POC run & evaluation plan — 1-week internal pilot (traffic replay) then 1-week staged canary in your preprod
4) Exec sync & commercial terms — aim for week of 4/29 once POC proves out

Can we confirm the POC window you prefer? We listed potential start dates in the attached deck (w/ resource estimates). I’ll also drop a HubSpot note with the mutual action plan.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priya — thanks for the clear write-up and the deck. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The latency targets you captured match our internal goals. For the short decisioning endpoint the business wants P95 <= 100ms if possible; if 120ms is the baseline we’ll accept that for the POC but would like an optimization path to 100ms.
- SOC2 point of contact is me (I’ll pull the current artifact bundle and share the link to our secure S3 by EOD Friday).
- For the POC start window: earliest we can commit infra for a replay run is 4/23 (we have capacity-team maintenance earlier in the month). 4/23–4/30 is our preferred 1-week window.

I’m attaching the security intake form we usually use for new infra vendors (small PDF). Also can you include an estimated token-cost delta for the POC (rough per-hour estimate) in the POC spec so our finance partner can pre-approve budget?

Thanks — Julia

Attachment: mosaic_security_intake.pdf

Julia — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few operational confirmations and what we’ll deliver Tuesday: 

Deliverables by 2029-04-16 (Tue)
- POC spec (hardware + model config + routing policy) including a cost estimate split by token-hours and GPU-hour proforma. We’ll call out the delta vs your current on-prem environment.
- Test plan for the traffic replay (we’ll provide a small harness and sample replay data)
- Runbook for the POC — expected monitoring dashboards and success criteria (P95/P99, error budget, token-cost per 1k responses)

Operational notes / assumptions we’re using in the cost estimate
- Model profile: LlamaX-13B quantized (4-bit), expected tokenization overhead 1.02x, average response 32 tokens
- Baseline burst model: sustained 60 qps for 1 hour/day with 3x short bursts up to 200 qps for 2–3 minutes each
- We will propose both a Dedicated GPU pool spec (for true isolation) and a Private-VPC-with-hosted-fallback topology; the POC can run in Private-VPC mode so you can validate networking and key management (KMS) without committing to reserved capacity

Security & compliance
- We can accept mosaic_security_intake.pdf via secure S3 link. For SOC2 artifacts we’ll provide the attestation summary and a list of log types we can surface during the POC (audit logs, trace ids, token-level latency breakdowns).

Scheduling
- We’ll hold tentative capacity for 4/23 start but will confirm final node sizing after the POC spec is approved early next week.

Next steps for finance/ops
- Priya / Kimberly will add the token-cost delta and rough budget to the POC spec. If Julia’s finance partner needs a formal quote we can route to our sales ops for a non-binding estimate.

I’ve also uploaded the POC checklist to the shared Drive link in the HubSpot task you’ll see shortly.

—Sean
